page.layout: One page of text, single column. Running head and page number at top. No marginal notes; the scriptural references sit inline at the start or end of lines. Below the text: a verse heading "VERSVS V." followed by one italic verse line.

main_text.p: Matth.9.28. Instrumento autem,id est fidei,in hoc & similibus dictis id tribuitur, quod proprium est causae efficientis principis,id est,Dei ipsius.
3. Quis autem dubitet, eo τῷ χαρίσματι [?] uinci desperationis paroxysmum, quod facit ut exstent quae sperantur, & quod demonstrat quae non uidentur:Fidei autem hoc proprium est.Heb.11.1.

4. Id quod mundum uincit,etiam tentationum,quae in mundo nos adoriuntur, παροξυσμοῖς [?] uincit.Sed,ut ait Ioanes:Quicquid natu est ex Deo,uincit mundū: & hęc est uictoria quae uicit mundum, nempe fides nostra. Quis est q uincit mundum,nisi qui credit Iesum esse Christum? 1.Ioan.5.4.5.

Det nobis Dominus noster Iesus Christus, ut cum in tentationes inciderimus varias, pro summo id ducamus gaudio; Iac.1.2, & ut sub pedibus nostris Satan cito conteratur: Rom.16.20. nobis videlicet omnibus plene de eo persuasis, quod Dominus noster dixit:Confidite,ego vici mundum.Ioan.16.33.
main_text.head: VERSVS V.

p.i: Obsederant me aquae usq; ad animam: abyssus

page.notes: The Greek words "τῷ χαρίσματι" and "παροξυσμοῖς" are hard to read at this scan resolution; both marked [?]. "q uicit" in the 1 Ioan. sentence is as printed and may be a misprint for "qui". The scriptural references (Matth., Heb., Ioan., Iac., Rom.) are run-in within the text column, not in a true margin, so they are kept inline. The verse line at the foot is partly cut off on the right and its last word "abyssus" is only partly legible; it is given as read, with the italic line marked as verse.
